problem: Open-vocabulary ObjectNav methods such as VLFM treat VLM cosine-similarity scores as point estimates from a single hand-tuned prompt, ignoring the semantic uncertainty caused by prompt phrasing. Small prompt changes alter navigation performance, so the pipelines are brittle and need prompt engineering.
motivation: VLM relevance scores vary with prompt wording (e.g. 'chair' vs 'a chair'), which makes exploration inconsistent and limits how well planners can use the scores. Modelling this uncertainty explicitly and planning with it should remove the need for hand-tuned prompts and let the planner trade off exploiting high-relevance frontiers against exploring uncertain ones.
key_idea: Estimate the mean and variance of VLM semantic relevance with a GPT-4-generated prompt ensemble, fuse them into a Bayesian (Gaussian) semantic relevance map, and choose frontiers with a multi-armed-bandit objective (expected improvement or GP-UCB).
insight: Prompt choice matters for the VLFM baseline: on HM3D, SR ranges from 50.60 to 53.20 across seven alternative prompts, against 52.60 for the default. A prompt ensemble with uncertainty-aware planning reaches similar SR (52.25 / 53.50) with no prompt tuning. QQ plots of 100 prompt-ensemble scores show they are approximately Gaussian, which supports the conjugate Gaussian map update. The uncertainty-seeking planning costs SPL, since the agent takes detours toward uncertain regions.
method: Detection and goal navigation: follows VLFM, using YOLOv7 plus Grounding DINO to detect the target, MobileSAM to segment it, the depth centroid as goal position, and DD-PPO for point-goal navigation.
Probabilistic sensor model: BLIP-2 cosine similarity between the image and N GPT-4-generated prompt variants gives a Gaussian (mu_Z, sigma_Z^2) over semantic relevance.
Viewpoint confidence: C_V(theta)=cos^2(2*theta*pi/theta_fov) is folded into the sensor variance, sigma_Z^2(theta)=sigma_Z^2+(1-C_V), so peripheral pixels are less certain.

Probabilistic semantic map: a 2D grid holds a Gaussian per cell (prior mean 0.5, variance 0.5) updated in closed form by a conjugate Gaussian (Kalman-style) update over the camera focal cone, alongside an occupancy obstacle map.
I-FBE1 planner: picks the frontier with the highest expected improvement over the best frontier mean, using the map mean and std.
I-FBE2 planner: picks the frontier with the highest GP-UCB score, mu+sqrt(beta)*sigma, which explores more aggressively.

setting.backbone: BLIP-2 (frozen) for relevance, GPT-4 for prompt generation, YOLOv7 + Grounding DINO + MobileSAM for detection, DD-PPO for point-goal navigation (all pretrained)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with known robot pose
setting.action_space: discrete low-level actions (move forward, turn left/right, stop) via DD-PPO to frontier or goal waypoints

results: I-FBE1 and I-FBE2 reach SR comparable to VLFM without hand-tuned prompts: HM3D 52.25 and 53.50 vs 52.60, and MP3D 35.26 and 35.63 vs 36.40. They beat ESC, ZSON, CoW and the geometric FBE baselines, but their SPL is consistently slightly lower than VLFM (HM3D 28.96 and 27.31 vs 30.40; MP3D 16.47 and 16.52 vs 17.50).
limitations: SPL is consistently below VLFM because the uncertainty-seeking planner takes detours to uncertain but not very relevant regions.
Replanning costs about 420 ms per timestep, and the method does not surpass VLFM on SR (I-FBE2 is only marginally higher on HM3D and lower on MP3D).
Evaluated only in simulation with known pose and no sensor noise; the Gaussian assumption is validated on only five images and a few categories.
